stages.headline: The midpoint of A(x₁; y₁)B(x₂; y₂) has coordinates equal to the half-sums of the ends' coordinates.
stages.headlineEnglish: The midpoint of A(x₁; y₁)B(x₂; y₂) has coordinates equal to the half-sums of the ends' coordinates.

stages.headline: Example: A(−2; 1), B(4; 3) give the midpoint C(1; 2).
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: A(−2; 1), B(4; 3) give the midpoint C(1; 2).

stages.headline: If the midpoint and one end are known, the other end is x₂ = 2x − x₁, y₂ = 2y − y₁.
stages.headlineEnglish: If the midpoint and one end are known, the other end is x₂ = 2x − x₁, y₂ = 2y − y₁.
